name: Data Cleaning Conventions
description: This module defines the naming, formatting, and structural style conventions to follow whenever writing, implementing, or reviewing data cleaning code or output, so results stay consistent with the existing data cleaning style guide.
content:
This module defines the naming, formatting, and structural style conventions to follow whenever writing, implementing, or reviewing data cleaning code or output, so results stay consistent with the existing data cleaning style guide.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Check that data cleaning terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
2. When multiple data cleaning strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
3. Keep data cleaning outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
4. Document any non-obvious data cleaning decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
5. Prefer explicit, readable data cleaning solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
6. Measure before optimizing any data cleaning bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
7. Prefer the simplest data cleaning approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
8. When data cleaning decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
9. Keep data cleaning changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of data cleaning correctness.
- Do not apply generic data cleaning advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not silently drop data cleaning edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these data cleaning guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
